text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin hints at possible taxes targetting corporate portfolio income.
-- German insurer Allianz chairman Henning Schulte-Noelle in German newspaper interview confirms his interest for insurer GAN, expected to be privatised.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Jospin does not rule out consulting the French people in debate on whether to favour employment or a strict compliance with the Maastricht treaty criteria.
-- Reform of the CDR company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets may resort to status including a supervisory board and a board of directors.
-- A final agreement on the shutdown of the Renault Vilvoorde assembly plant to be signed Monday, it excludes outright layoffs.
-- National Statistics Institute INSEE forecasts 2.3 percent GDP growth rate for 1997, same as previous government's forecast.
L'AGEFI
-- Savings banks Caisses d'Epargne and Natexis bank to create subsidiaries in the invoicing business.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government considers targetting well-off households and businesses' profits from capital gains with new taxes in order to reduce the public deficit.
-- TF1 TV channel expects 213 million francs in 1998 additional earnings from longer advertising time authorised by audio-visual authority CSA.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Jospin calls for time to consider how to create jobs.
-- Employment and Solidarity Minister Martine Aubry told Senate plans to change Robien law on cuts in labour charges for companies hiring new staff.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- LVMH shares rise on talk of merger of liquor business with that of GrandMet and Guinness.
